subject: Price precision: modular bundle vs consumption assessment
content:
From: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@novazoom.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@novazoom.com
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarification on packaging: modular bundles vs consumption pricing

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — product looked solid. Before we move deeper I need to get our procurement team aligned on the commercial shape. Two quick, practical asks: 1) can you show (side-by-side) an example P&L for a mid-usage customer under a modular bundle (seat + reserved capacity) vs pure consumption (on-demand tokens)? and 2) what are the discount thresholds if we commit to a 12-month reserved capacity?

We're primarily concerned about predictable unit economics during a growth surge (2–3x over six months). If there are ways to convert unused reserved capacity into credits or temporary seat reductions, that would help our CFO sign off.

I can loop in procurement if you need a formal worksheet.

Appreciate it —
Tom Hayes
Head of Platform
NovaZoom

---

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@novazoom.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, procurement@novazoom.com
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarification on packaging: modular bundles vs consumption pricing

Tom — thanks, glad the demo was useful. I pulled together a concise comparison and an editable workbook (attached) that models three scenarios:

- Small steady state (25k tokens/day)
- Growth surge (75k tokens/day by month 6)
- Spiky bursts (daily peaks at 150k tokens for short windows)

Key summary:
- Modular bundle (seats + reserved capacity): lower headline cost per token at predictable throughput; best if 60–80% of capacity is utilized. We offer an annual tiered discount that reaches up to 22% at higher commitments.
- Consumption (on-demand): simpler operationally; unit cost per token ~20–35% higher at scale but no upfront reserve. Better for very spiky workloads.

We support a 6–12 month credit conversion for unused reserved capacity (applies as platform credits) and a one-time flexible seat swap within the first 90 days of the term. That policy is in the attached playbook.

Attached: pricing_model_v2.xlsx (workbook), modular_bundle_playbook.pdf (policy + sample contract clause).

Next steps I suggest: 1) you and procurement take a look at the workbook; 2) we run a quick sensitivity call to pin an expected utilization curve — I can bring Jonas for runtime and cache impact. Available Fri 9/11 10:00–12:00 PT or Mon 9/14 afternoon.

Best,

—
Soojin Lee
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on packaging: modular bundles vs consumption pricing

Quick technical note on the workbook: the effective cost per useful token depends heavily on cache hit rate and inference sequence length distribution. For NovaZoom's demo traces (we sampled 2 days), the KV cache shows ~28% token reduction on repeated prompts; that pushes the modular bundle economics further in your favor because reserved capacity is amortized over more effective tokens.

Also: if you expect bursty peaks, consider assigning a small burst credit pool (we can size it) rather than full headroom; that keeps commitment lower but provides a safety valve for 24–48h spikes.

Happy to walk through the math on the call.

—Jonas
Principal Infra Eng, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Hi Soojin —

Thanks for the workbook. Two procurement questions: 1) we need clarity on the rollback clause if NovaZoom needs to reduce committed capacity mid-term (detailed % and notice requirements), and 2) is there a standard Service Credit for availability outages tied to reserved capacity? Please point us to the clause in the playbook.

Also please confirm whether the 22% discount band is on reserved compute only or total invoice (compute + inference platform features).

Procurement
NovaZoom

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: procurement@novazoom.com, Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@novazoom.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on packaging: modular bundles vs consumption pricing

Hi — good questions. Short answers inline below; happy to add contract language to the playbook and share a tracked version.

1) Rollback / reduction: we support a stepped reduction of committed capacity once per 6-month window with a 30-day notice. Reductions below 50% of initial commit trigger a pro-rated early reduction fee (detailed formula in playbook section 3.2). We can add a one-time carveout for the first term for NovaZoom (i.e., one mid-term reduction without fee) as part of a standard 12-month commitment.

2) Service credits: availability SLA is in the SOW appendix. For reserved capacity outages that materially impact throughput, we provide service credits tied to missed throughput SLOs (rather than pure uptime). I'll attach the exact clause in the updated playbook.

3) Discount scope: the 22% headline applies to reserved compute only; platform feature fees (observability retention, advanced support) are discounted at 10% in that band. We can create an all-in blended discount schedule for the term if that helps procurement modeling.

Action items:
- I'll produce a tracked-playbook with the rollback clause and an appendix with the sample credit calculation (ETA: Mon 9/14).
- Jonas and I are available Mon 9/14 1:00–3:00 PM PT for the sensitivity call if that works.

If you prefer a short 30-min call first to confirm modeling assumptions, we can do Fri 9/11 10:30 PT.

Thanks,

—
Soojin Lee
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
